title: Overnight SIEM alerts: brute force, password spraying and impossible travel
situation: Our security monitoring system collected 52 log events overnight from sign-in, firewall, DNS (domain name system), endpoint and application sources. Several point to attacks on user accounts: repeated failed logins followed by a success, one address trying many accounts, and users signing in from two continents within an hour. We also suspect noisy alerts and a gap where one log source went quiet.
your_task: Correlate the 52 events into alerts using the detection rules.
Apply the suppression list, but only entries that have an owner and have not expired.
Write the response for each alert, such as disable the account, revoke sessions or quarantine the host.
Measure alert quality before and after tuning, and name any attack that no rule caught.
why_it_matters: A successful login right after a burst of failures may mean an attacker is already inside an account. Too many false alarms bury the real ones, and a silent log source is a blind spot.
done_when: All 12 alerts have a disposition, a reason and a response.
Only the owned, unexpired scanner suppression is applied; the expired and ownerless ones are ignored.

Account alerts (brute force on jdoe, spraying, impossible travel for bnguyen and asmith, after-hours admin grant by mlee) are handed to the Identity and Access Management (IAM) team for account disable, session revocation, multi-factor authentication (MFA) checks and access review.
The missed low-and-slow password guessing against pchan is logged as a detection gap.

glossary.SIEM: Security information and event management: a system that gathers logs and raises alerts.
glossary.Correlation rule: Logic that links related events, such as five failed logins in five minutes.
glossary.Brute force: Trying many passwords against one account.
glossary.Password spraying: Trying one or two common passwords against many accounts.
glossary.Impossible travel: Sign-ins from places too far apart to reach in the time between them.
glossary.Suppression: A rule that silences a known, harmless alert; it should have an owner and an end date.
glossary.Precision / recall: Precision is the share of alerts that were real; recall is the share of real attacks that raised an alert.

talking_point: Correlated 52 log events into 12 alerts, suppressed 1 authorized-scanner false positive to raise precision from 83.3% to 90.9%, sent the brute-force, spraying and impossible-travel account alerts to IAM for session revocation and MFA checks, and flagged a missed low-and-slow password attack as a detection gap.
